plans.objective: [DIM: composition] The Ca/Si/Al/O stoichiometry of the glass network controls the defect density of structural voids, which in turn modulates the effective activation energy for ion migration via a percolation threshold.

steps.description: The hypothesis proposes a percolation-based relationship between Ca/Si/Al/O composition, structural void density, and ion migration activation energy in glass. This requires a materials design exploration across compositional space. I will generate a series of glass network compositions, simulate their atomic structures using MD to quantify void density and ion migration barriers, and identify the percolation threshold where activation energy changes abruptly. The goal is to map composition → void density → activation energy and validate the percolation mechanism.
